Subject: RFP: Data training exclusions — evidence and retention windows

Priya,

Thanks for taking our RFP questions. As part of procurement we need written confirmation and operational detail for the following items before we move to legal review: 

1) A statement confirming you do not use customer-provided production data to train or fine-tune any models (including upstream derivation). If you make any isolated exceptions, list them.
2) For hosted and dedicated deployments: retention windows for request logs, KV caches, generation traces, telemetry, and backups/snapshots. Clarify what is accessible to Redwood staff vs. automatically purged.
3) Deletion SLA: when a customer requests account-level deletion or a data purge, how long until data is removed from active stores, from backups, and from any analytics/observability pipelines?
4) Evidence: examples of artifacts you can provide (signed statement, retention matrix, sample audit log export, SOC2/ISO references).

We prefer concise operational answers (times, policies, and where exceptions exist). Please attach any short artifacts. Our legal team will push on exact wording, so we may follow up with redlines.

From: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: RFP: Data training exclusions — evidence and retention windows

Hi Olivia — thanks for the clear list. Short answers first, then a concise operational breakdown below. Attached: redwood-training-exclusion-statement.pdf (signed product statement), retention-matrix.csv, and a simplified llm-data-flow-diagram.png. HubSpot record HS-8721 will track follow-ups.

Summary answers:
- Training: Redwood does NOT use customer production data to train or fine-tune our public or internal models for hosted or Dedicated offerings. We also do not create derivative training datasets from customer inputs.
- Private deployments: for VPC/on-prem customers Redwood does not have access to customer data; no training, period.
- Telemetry & aggregates: we collect anonymized service telemetry (latency, error rates) and aggregate usage statistics for platform health and product improvement. This telemetry is sampled and aggregated; it contains no customer PII or full prompt/response content.
- Retention windows (typical defaults): request logs (searchable request/response metadata) — 30 days; short-lived KV cache/attention caches — ephemeral per request and cleared on completion; generation traces (full text) — retained only if explicitly enabled by customer (default: disabled); backups/snapshots/s3 object versions — retained 90 days by default; audit logs (admin events) — 365 days (retainable longer as an add-on).
- Deletion SLA: account-level purge request -> objects flagged and removed from active indexes within 48 hours; removal from primary storage follows within 7 days; backups and immutable snapshots: rotated/overwritten within 90 days; audit/legal holds supersede deletion until release. For Dedicated customers we provide a deletion certificate when the purge completes.

Operational notes (details):
1) "We do not train" scope: applies to any customer content processed by Redwood's hosted and Dedicated inference endpoints. The only exceptions are opt-in programs (none currently in production) where a customer explicitly agrees to share labeled data for model evaluation; those are governed by a separate Data Contribution Agreement and require explicit sign-off.

2) Where data may transiently exist: the serving runtime maintains an in-memory KV cache for active sessions; that cache is ephemeral and never persisted to long-term training stores. Short traces used for debugging are only captured when a customer enables debug mode; they are stored behind role-based access and are purged on request per the deletion SLA.

3) Backups and snapshots: daily service snapshots are encrypted (KMS) and subject to our snapshot retention policy (default 90 days). For Dedicated customers we also support customer-managed snapshot rotation and S3 lifecycle rules.

4) Evidence we can provide: signed product statement (attached), CSV retention matrix (attached), sample audit log export (redacted), SOC 2 Type II report summary (available under NDA), and for Private deployments a short architecture note showing no egress from customer VPC.

5) Legal hold and export: legal/process holds will delay deletion; we will surface the hold and work with FinServ Legal on scope.

If useful, Michael can join a short call to walk through the retention matrix and share a redacted audit export.

Best,

Priya Natarajan
